properties.natural_language: Buffer read requests from opcode callers must provide a non-negative offset and size, and the buffer reference must be a valid memory region.
Memory write operations must receive a valid position (U256) and value (bytes) where position + len(value) does not overflow U256 arithmetic.
Memory expansion gas costs are always charged before any write operation modifies memory contents.
Position parameters of type U256 are bounded by gas economics: memory expansion gas cost grows quadratically, making positions beyond practical memory limits economically infeasible.
Buffer reads beyond buffer boundaries return zero-padded data of exactly the requested size, never exposing uninitialized memory.
After a memory write completes, the memory region [position, position+len(value)) contains exactly the written bytes.
After a memory read completes, the returned bytes are an exact copy of memory[position:position+size] with no side effects on memory contents.
EVM memory is always initialized as an empty bytearray at the start of each execution context; no data leaks between calls.
Memory expansion gas cost is always charged before the memory operation executes; if gas is insufficient, the operation reverts without modifying memory.
URL path components received from external users must be validated against expected patterns (/block/*, /tx/*, /address/*, /token/*) before routing to data fetch handlers.
Resource identifiers extracted from URL paths (block hashes, tx hashes, addresses) must be validated for correct format (hex encoding, length, checksum) before use in database queries.
The /block/ endpoint must accept both block hashes (0x-prefixed 64-char hex) and block heights (decimal integers) as valid identifiers.
When a requested resource (block, tx, address, token) does not exist, the explorer returns an HTTP 404 response.

When redirect is required for backward compatibility, the generated redirect URL correctly maps the standard path to the explorer's internal URL format without introducing open redirect vulnerabilities.
The block explorer displays accurate blockchain data matching the identifiers provided in the URL; data integrity is preserved from source to display.
Before any PUSH operation, sufficient gas (GAS_BASE for PUSH0, GAS_VERY_LOW for PUSH1-32) must be available; if not, execution halts with out-of-gas error.
After a PUSHn operation completes, the stack height increases by exactly 1 and the program counter advances by 1+n bytes.
DUP operations must verify stack depth before accessing the target item; if item_number >= len(stack), a StackUnderflowError is raised.
After a DUP operation completes successfully, the stack height increases by exactly 1 and the duplicated value equals the original at position item_number.
SWAP operations must verify stack depth before exchanging values; if item_number >= len(stack), a StackUnderflowError is raised.
After a SWAP operation completes, stack[0] contains the original value at position item_number and stack[item_number] contains the original stack[0]; all other positions are unchanged.
The EVM stack depth must never exceed 1024 items; PUSH and DUP operations that would exceed this limit raise StackOverflowError.
EVM bytecode is immutable during execution; PUSH instructions always read the same immediate bytes regardless of execution state.
The EVM stack maintains correct ordering where position 0 is always the top of the stack throughout all operations.
After a POP operation, the stack height decreases by exactly 1 and the previously second item is now at position 0.
Chain switch requests from DApps via wallet_updateEthereumChain must have chainId in 0x-prefixed EIP-155 format; malformed chainId must be rejected.
RPC URLs provided in chain switch requests must pass SSRF prevention: localhost, private IP ranges (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x), and link-local addresses must be blocked.
RPC URLs must use HTTPS protocol; HTTP URLs must be rejected during sanitization.
Before accepting a DApp-provided RPC endpoint, the wallet must verify that both net_version and eth_chainId responses match the claimed chain parameters.
Chain switch requests referencing known chain names but with non-matching parameters must trigger phishing detection warnings to the user.
User confirmation is always required before any chain switch operation; no DApp request can bypass the user approval dialog.
After user rejection of a chain switch, error code 4001 is returned to the DApp and the wallet remains on the original chain.
Chain switching only changes the active chain for the current DApp session, not the wallet's persistent default configuration.
Builder bids received via execution_payload_bid gossip must have valid cryptographic signatures before any other validation steps.
Builder bid amount must not exceed the builder's on-chain balance; bids with insufficient balance coverage must be rejected.
Builder bids must reference the correct parent block hash matching the proposer's current chain head view.
Attestation data.index field in Gloas must be exactly 0 (payload absent) or 1 (payload present); any other value is invalid.
If no valid builder bids are received before the proposal deadline, the proposer must fall back to local block construction.
After successful bid validation, the selected builder bid is included in the SignedBeaconBlock along with aggregated payload attestations (up to MAX_PAYLOAD_ATTESTATIONS).
PTC members must wait until 75% of the slot (PAYLOAD_ATTESTATION_DUE_BPS = 7500) before creating PayloadAttestationMessages.
RPC requests for uncle block data must provide valid block hash format and uncle index; malformed inputs must not cause crashes or information leakage.
For blocks at or after EIP-1559 activation, the uncle block RPC response must include the baseFee field with the correct Quantity-typed value from the block header.
For blocks before EIP-1559 activation, the uncle block RPC response must omit the baseFee field entirely.
The EIP-1559 activation block boundary is consistently applied across all client implementations for determining baseFee field presence.
The baseFee value returned in uncle block responses is the actual consensus-validated baseFee from the block header.
An EIP's lifecycle state transitions are monotonic: once an EIP moves to 'Scheduled' or 'Declined', it cannot revert to 'Proposed' or 'Considered' within the same upgrade cycle.
Network upgrade activation follows strict ordering: testnets (Sepolia, Holesky) activate before mainnet.
An EIP must pass initial evaluation review before moving to 'Considered for Inclusion' status.
All 48-byte inputs to KZG operations must be validated as valid BLS12-381 G1 points: check for point at infinity special case (0xc0 + 47 zero bytes), then full BLS validation for non-infinity points.
All 32-byte field element inputs must be less than the BLS modulus (52435875175126190479447740508185965837690552500527637822603658699938581184513); values at or above the modulus must be rejected.
Proof verification inputs must have exact byte lengths (commitment: 48B, z: 32B, y: 32B, proof: 48B) before any cryptographic operations are performed.
After KZG commitment to versioned hash conversion, the result is exactly 32 bytes with version byte 0x01 prepended to the truncated SHA256 hash.
The trusted setup parameter KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL_1 used in pairing checks is immutable and matches the ceremony-generated value.
A valid KZG proof verification (pairing check equals FQ12.one()) confirms that the polynomial committed to by the commitment evaluates to y at point z.
Incoming transactions must be type-detected by inspecting the first byte: legacy (RLP list prefix), 0x01 (EIP-2930), or 0x02 (EIP-1559); unknown type prefixes must be rejected.
EIP-1559 transactions must satisfy max_fee_per_gas >= current base_fee_per_gas; transactions violating this condition must be rejected.
For EIP-1559 transactions, the effective gas price is correctly computed as min(max_priority_fee, max_fee - base_fee) + base_fee.
The base fee adjustment per block is bounded to a maximum of 12.5% (1/8) increase or decrease from the parent block's base fee.
When parent gas_used equals target gas (gas_limit/2), the base fee for the next block equals the parent's base fee exactly.
Gas refund is capped at 20% of gas consumed (London reduction from 50%); actual refund = min(refund_counter, gas_consumed * 20%).
After access list processing, all declared addresses are marked 'warm' (reduced access cost) and all declared storage keys are marked 'warm' (reduced SLOAD cost).
Access list gas cost is correctly computed as (addresses * 2400) + (storage_keys * 1900) and added to intrinsic gas.
The base fee portion of transaction fees is burned (removed from total supply); only the priority fee is paid to the block producer.
All DataColumnSidecars received via gossip must have KZG proofs verified against known commitments before acceptance into the local data store.
Column data received via req/resp fallback must undergo the same KZG proof verification as gossip-received data; invalid proofs must be rejected.
Data recovery requires at least 50% of columns (64 of 128) with valid KZG proofs before Reed-Solomon reconstruction can begin.
Custody group assignment is deterministic based on node-id: given the same node-id, the same set of custody groups is always computed.
The set of verified columns for a given block is monotonically non-decreasing throughout the sampling process; verified columns are never removed.
After full matrix recovery, all 128 columns have been reconstructed and the node may cross-seed reconstructed sidecars to the network.
Each node custodies at least CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT (4) custody groups, ensuring minimum participation in data availability.
Column-to-custody-group mapping follows the formula: column_index = NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS * i + custody_group, producing a uniform distribution.
After buffer bounds check, if offset + size <= buffer length, the read proceeds without zero-padding; otherwise zero-padding is applied.
Memory expansion calculation determines whether the operation's target address exceeds the current memory high-water mark.
URL path parsing correctly routes requests to the appropriate handler: /block/* to block fetch, /tx/* to tx fetch, /address/* to address fetch, /token/* to token fetch.
Backward-compatible explorers check native route support and either serve content directly or generate a redirect response.
Data fetch actions (block, tx, address, token) all result in a rendered page returned to the user.
Redirect responses include the HTTP 301/302 status with the correctly constructed internal URL.
POP operation requires at least one item on the stack; if the stack is empty, a StackUnderflowError is raised.
DUP gas (GAS_VERY_LOW) is charged before stack depth check; SWAP gas (GAS_VERY_LOW) is charged before swap depth check.
Successful DUP reads the value at the nth position and pushes a copy to the top.
Stack underflow in DUP or SWAP raises StackUnderflowError and halts execution.
SWAP with sufficient depth exchanges values at position 0 and position item_number atomically.
PUSH reads N immediate bytes from bytecode and converts them to big-endian U256.
RPC URL validation calls net_version then eth_chainId in sequence to verify endpoint correctness.
When chain is unknown, user is prompted to add the new chain before switching.
After chain switch, wallet emits appropriate events and updates active chain to new chainId.
SSRF check must block internal targets before proceeding to chain list verification.
Proposer preferences broadcast includes fee_recipient and gas_limit via gossip network.
Builder bid validation proceeds sequentially: balance check, parent hash verification, signature verification.
Payload attestations are aggregated up to MAX_PAYLOAD_ATTESTATIONS for block inclusion.
Attestation at 25% slot checks fork-choice for payload presence to set data.index field.
Fork state determination correctly classifies blocks relative to EIP-1559 activation boundary.
Uncle block validation checks baseFee requirement based on block position relative to EIP-1559 fork.
RPC response is returned to the client after proper construction.
EIP evaluation is a prerequisite for both approval and decline decisions.
Activation configuration produces distinct timestamps per network (Sepolia, Holesky, Mainnet).
G1 point at infinity is accepted without further BLS validation as a valid special case.
After input conversion to cryptographic types, both G2 (X-z) and G1 (P-y) computations proceed in parallel for the pairing check.
Type conversion from raw bytes to KZG types succeeds only after length validation passes.
Versioned hash creation: SHA256 hash of commitment is computed, then version byte 0x01 prepended.
Base fee increases when parent gas_used exceeds target; decrease proportional formula using integer division.
Legacy and EIP-2930 transactions use gas_price directly as effective gas price.
Gas refund is calculated then applied: effective_gas_used = gas_consumed - min(refund_counter, gas_consumed*20%), remainder returned to sender.
Access list gas includes per-address cost (2400) and per-storage-key cost (1900) added to intrinsic gas.
After selecting sample groups, missing columns are requested via req/resp from custody peers.
Column indices map correctly to custody groups via formula, and node subscribes to matching gossip subnets.
After recovery, cross-seeding exposes reconstructed sidecars to subscribed peers to aid network-wide availability.
